remainingLocalWork.item: AS-PAR-009 — Pricing review, evidence-bound dispatch and client response
remainingLocalWork.details: Committed at cee546f9 (2026-10-10): versioned firm pricing policy per currency with a distinct second rule administrator (fee band, optional discount cap, validity window) bounding new quotations; append-only quotation-approval revocations that block dispatch and acceptance until a fresh approval; quotation validity expiry enforced at dispatch and acceptance; acceptance requires the signatory email and it must match the dispatch recipient or the lead primary contact; commercial mail receipt states QUEUED/DISPATCHED/PROVIDER_ACCEPTED/REJECTED/UNKNOWN with a database guard that keeps a provider-verified receipt terminal; Angular pricing-policy, revocation and receipt views; migration 20261010185946_CommercialPricingPolicyAndDeliveryReceipts. remainingLocalWork.item: FSR-002 / FSR-010 / FSR-011 first slice — typed statement presentation as genuine PDF, Word and Excel (unapproved draft)
remainingLocalWork.details:

review.method: Read-only adversarial review by three independent lenses (truthfulness, authorization and exposure, Angular contract and accessibility); each finding was verified against source before action.
fixedInThisSlice: Advance card and activation readiness now use the milestone PAID state that activation checks, not an allocation total that credit notes can inflate.
The advance is read only from a fee agreement linked to this engagement; an unlinked agreement reports NOT_LINKED, as activation refuses it.
The letter card requires the letter template, commercial profile and firm seal, in the order the letter command refuses them.
A route mismatch between the proposal and the engagement blocks the letter and reports ROUTE_MISMATCH.
Readiness requires a firm-wide grant, so an engagement-only grant cannot read client-level Partner decisions or the decider's name.
Letter and activation actions are server-computed flags (canGenerateLetter, canActivate) for the requesting actor, not inferred in the browser.
The stage 4 advance blocker is listed only while the advance is unpaid.
The engagement's proposal is the one its linked fee agreement binds, falling back to the client's newest proposal only when none is linked.
The workflow route allowlist no longer admits dot segments.

READY_FOR_REVIEW is shown as pending, not as a success state; phases carry visible status text, list semantics and canonical-order validation; 401 ends the session and 403 says the panel is unavailable to the role.
openDecisionsOrDeferred: The protected letter guard applies offer identity only when a dispatch record exists; the read model additionally requires the sent and response offer hashes to match. Hardening the command is an owner decision and was not changed in this slice.
FeeAgreementWorkspaceQuery.CanCreate does not repeat the quotation-revision check of the create command (pre-existing; this file is not in the slice).
With no linked fee agreement, the engagement is bound to the client's newest proposal; a newer draft for another route can hide a cleared engagement until a fee agreement is linked.
The readiness read does not pass the automatic advance-invoice setting, so the preparation message can read as drafting disabled when it is enabled.
The workflow card shows lifecycle blocker text to every role that the lifecycle endpoint already accepts; this is an existing exposure, now more prominent.
Non-permission refusals (projection and reconciliation gates) map to HTTP 403, following the existing UI read pattern.
The shared instant decoder accepts timestamps without an offset (pre-existing decoder).
No automated test drives a fully paid advance through receipt allocation; the PAID branch relies on the same milestone predicate that ActivateAsync checks, verified by code reading.
